text: Man is the only creature who refuses to be what he is.
author: Albert Camus

text: A nihilist is not one who believes in nothing, but one who does not believe in what exists.
author: Albert Camus

text: What is a rebel? A man who says no.
author: Albert Camus

text: Knowing whether or not one can live without appeal is all that interests me.
author: Albert Camus

text: We have exiled beauty; the Greeks took up arms for her.
author: Albert Camus

text: We get into the habit of living before acquiring the habit of thinking.
author: Albert Camus

text: There are more things to admire in men than to despise.
author: Albert Camus

text: The most elementary form of rebellion, paradoxically, expresses an aspiration for order.
author: Albert Camus

text: The struggle itself toward the heights is enough to fill a man's heart. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
author: Albert Camus

text: I wish that every human life might be pure transparent freedom.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: What is an adult? A child puffed with age.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: There is only one good. And that is to act according to the dictates of one's conscience.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: If you live long enough, you'll see that every victory turns into a defeat.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: I am incapable of conceiving infinity, and yet I do not accept finity. I want this adventure that is the context of my life to go on without end.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: One's life has value so long as one attributes value to the life of others, by means of love, friendship, indignation and compassion.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: One is not born a genius, one becomes a genius; and the feminine situation has up to the present rendered this becoming practically impossible.
author: Simone de Beauvoir

text: We are what we pretend to be, so we must be careful about what we pretend to be.
author: Kurt Vonnegut
source: Mother Night (1962), introduction to the 1966 edition

text: This is my principal objection to life, I think: It is too easy, when alive, to make perfectly horrible mistakes.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: Just because some of us can read and write and do a little math, that doesn't mean we deserve to conquer the Universe.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: We are healthy only to the extent that our ideas are humane.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: Our awareness is all that is alive and maybe sacred in any of us. Everything else about us is dead machinery.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: History is merely a list of surprises.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: Belief is nearly the whole of the Universe, whether based on truth or not.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: And a step backward, after making a wrong turn, is a step in the right direction.
author: Kurt Vonnegut

text: If liberty means anything at all, it means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear.
author: George Orwell

text: To see what is in front of one's nose needs a constant struggle.
author: George Orwell
source: In Front of Your Nose, Tribune (22 March 1946)

text: The opinion that art should have nothing to do with politics is itself a political attitude.
author: George Orwell

text: Everyone believes in the atrocities of the enemy and disbelieves in those of his own side, without ever bothering to examine the evidence.
author: George Orwell
source: Looking Back on the Spanish War (1942)

text: Perhaps a man really dies when his brain stops, when he loses the power to take in a new idea.
author: George Orwell

text: The quickest way of ending a war is to lose it.
author: George Orwell

text: Beauty is meaningless until it is shared.
author: George Orwell

text: Society has always to demand a little more from human beings than it will get in practice.
author: George Orwell

text: Inside the word "emergency" is "emerge"; from an emergency new things come forth. The old certainties are crumbling fast, but danger and possibility are sisters.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: Joy doesn't betray but sustains activism.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: A better world, yes; a perfect world, never.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: when you face a politics that aspires to make you fearful, alienated and isolated, joy is a fine act of insurrection.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: What lies ahead seems unlikely; when it becomes the past, it seems inevitable.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: The ability to tell your own story, in words or images, is already a victory, already a revolt.
author: Rebecca Solnit

text: Language can erase, distort, point in the wrong direction, throw out decoys and distractions. It can bury the bodies or uncover them.
author: Rebecca Solnit
source: Call Them by Their True Names (2018)

text: If you are opposed to war, you are not a fringe minority. You are not a silent majority. You are part of a silenced majority. Silenced by the mainstream media.
author: Amy Goodman

text: We are a compassionate people. But people cannot take action if they don't have accurate information.
author: Amy Goodman

text: Hope lies in fighting back.
author: Amy Goodman

text: Those who are scorned today are tomorrow's visionaries.
author: Amy Goodman

text: We need a media that covers power, not covers for power.
author: Amy Goodman

text: I believe the media can be the greatest force for peace on Earth. Instead, all too often, it is wielded as a weapon of war.
author: Amy Goodman

text: We need to hear these silenced voices. That is the power of independent media: to give voice to the voiceless; to those who have been shut out of the debate.
author: Amy Goodman

text: Our responsibility in independent media is to cover the entire discussion, from the suites to the streets.
author: Amy Goodman

text: You get freedom by letting your enemy know that you'll do anything to get your freedom; then you'll get it. It's the only way you'll get it.
author: Malcolm X
source: Advice to the Youth of Mississippi (31 December 1964)

text: How can you thank a man for giving you what's already yours? How then can you thank him for giving you only part of what's already yours?
author: Malcolm X

text: I have no mercy or compassion in me for a society that will crush people, and then penalize them for not being able to stand up under the weight.
author: Malcolm X

text: People don't realize how a man's whole life can be changed by one book.
author: Malcolm X

text: You can't separate peace from freedom, because no one can be at peace unless he has his freedom.
author: Malcolm X
source: Speech in New York City (7 January 1965)

text: Power in defense of freedom is greater than power in behalf of tyranny and oppression.
author: Malcolm X

text: To me the earth's most explosive and pernicious evil is racism, the inability of God's creatures to live as One, especially in the Western world.
author: Malcolm X

text: The life of a single human being is worth a million times more than all the property of the richest man on earth.
author: Che Guevara

text: Far more important than a good remuneration is the pride of serving one's neighbor.
author: Che Guevara

text: Much more definitive and much more lasting than all the gold that one can accumulate is the gratitude of a people.
author: Che Guevara

text: The ultimate and most important revolutionary aspiration: to see human beings liberated from their alienation.
author: Che Guevara

text: Many will call me an adventurer, and that I am... only one of a different sort: one who risks his skin to prove his truths.
author: Che Guevara

text: The basic clay of our work is the youth; we place our hope in it and prepare it to take the banner from our hands.
author: Che Guevara

text: At the risk of seeming ridiculous, let me say that the true revolutionary is guided by a great feeling of love.
author: Che Guevara

text: Our responsibility is much greater than we might have supposed, because it involves all mankind.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
source: Existentialism and Human Emotions (1957 English edition)

text: I hate victims who respect their executioners.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: The past is the luxury of proprietors.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: For an occurrence to become an adventure, it is necessary and sufficient for one to recount it.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: Man is condemned to be free; because once thrown into the world, he is responsible for everything he does.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: What do I care about Jupiter? Justice is a human issue, and I do not need a god to teach it to me.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: If literature isn't everything, it's not worth a single hour of someone's trouble.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre

text: It belongs to the imperfection of everything human that man can only attain his desire by passing through its opposite.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: To stand on one leg and prove God's existence is a very different thing from going on one's knees and thanking Him.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: The tyrant dies and his rule is over; the martyr dies and his rule begins.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: Most men pursue pleasure with such breathless haste that they hurry past it.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: The truth is a trap: you can not get it without it getting you; you cannot get the truth by capturing it, only by its capturing you.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: Concepts, like individuals, have their histories, and are just as incapable of withstanding the ravages of time as are individuals.
author: Søren Kierkegaard

text: Revolutions are the locomotives of history.
author: Karl Marx
source: The Class Struggles in France, 1848 to 1850 (1850)

text: The foundation of irreligious criticism is: Man makes religion, religion does not make man.
author: Karl Marx
source: Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right (1843)

text: A man cannot become a child again, or he becomes childish.
author: Karl Marx

text: Reason has always existed, but not always in a rational form.
author: Karl Marx

text: Only that position can impart dignity in which we do not appear as servile tools but rather create independently within our circle.
author: Karl Marx
source: Reflections of a Youth on Choosing an Occupation (1835)

text: Men make their own history, but they do not make it as they please; they do not make it under self-selected circumstances, but under circumstances existing already, given and transmitted from the past.
author: Karl Marx
source: The Eighteenth Brumaire of Louis Bonaparte (1852)

text: Religion is the sigh of the oppressed creature, the heart of a heartless world, and the soul of soulless conditions.
author: Karl Marx
source: Contribution to the Critique of Hegel's Philosophy of Right (1843)

text: Freedom is always and exclusively freedom for the one who thinks differently.
author: Rosa Luxemburg

text: Historically, the errors committed by a truly revolutionary movement are infinitely more fruitful than the infallibility of the cleverest Central Committee.
author: Rosa Luxemburg

text: Without the collapse of capitalism the expropriation of the capitalist class is impossible.
author: Rosa Luxemburg

text: Bourgeois class domination is undoubtedly an historical necessity, but, so too, the rising of the working class against it.
author: Rosa Luxemburg

text: I’m a pessimist because of intelligence, but an optimist because of will.
author: Antonio Gramsci

text: All men are intellectuals: but not all men have in society the function of intellectuals.
author: Antonio Gramsci

text: History is at once freedom and necessity.
author: Antonio Gramsci

text: The quality of our life depends on the quality of the seeds that lie deep in our consciousness.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Freedom from suffering is a great happiness.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: It's wonderful to be alive and to walk on earth.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: Reality is reality. It transcends every concept. There is no concept which can adequately describe it, not even the concept of interdependence.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: To think in terms of either pessimism or optimism oversimplifies the truth. The problem is to see reality as it is.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: The present moment contains past and future. The secret of transformation, is in the way we handle this very moment.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh

text: You are a miracle, and everything you touch could be a miracle.
author: Thich Nhat Hanh
source: Speaking of Faith, National Public Radio (2003)

text: Fear is a natural reaction to moving closer to the truth.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Life is a good teacher and a good friend. Things are always in transition, if we could only realize it.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Every day, at the moment when things get edgy, we can just ask ourselves, “Am I going to practice peace, or am I going to war?”
author: Pema Chödrön

text: This very moment is the perfect teacher, and, lucky for us, it’s with us wherever we are.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Meditation is just gently coming back again and again to what's right here.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: We can't control what's going to happen but we can grow in awareness of what is happening.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: The experience of a sad and tender heart is what gives birth to fearlessness.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Meditation is an invitation to notice when we reach our limit and to not get carried away by hope and fear.
author: Pema Chödrön

text: Not everything that is faced can be changed; but nothing can be changed until it is faced.
author: James Baldwin
source: As Much Truth As One Can Bear, The New York Times Book Review (1962)

text: Nothing is more unbearable, once one has it, than freedom.
author: James Baldwin

text: Anyone who has ever struggled with poverty knows how extremely expensive it is to be poor.
author: James Baldwin

text: Nobody is more dangerous than he who imagines himself pure in heart; for his purity, by definition, is unassailable.
author: James Baldwin
source: The Black Boy Looks at the White Boy (1961)

text: If you don't know what happened behind you, you've no idea of what is happening around you.
author: James Baldwin

text: I think that mankind can do better than that, and I wish to be a witness to this small and stubborn possibility.
author: James Baldwin

text: Love does not begin and end the way we seem to think it does. Love is a battle, love is a war; love is a growing up.
author: James Baldwin

text: Whatever white people do not know about Negroes reveals, precisely and inexorably, what they do not know about themselves.
author: James Baldwin

text: Prisons do not disappear problems, they disappear human beings.
author: Angela Davis

text: Particularly in the United States, race has always played a central role in constructing presumptions of criminality.
author: Angela Davis

text: The vicious circle linking poverty, police, courts and prison is an integral element of ghetto existence.
author: Angela Davis
source: If They Come in the Morning (1971)

text: Progressive art can assist people to learn not only about the objective forces at work in the society in which they live, but also about the intensely social character of their interior lives.
author: Angela Davis
source: For a People's Culture, Political Affairs (March 1995)

text: It is the great challenge of our time: How to achieve justice, with struggle, but without war.
author: Howard Zinn

text: There is no flag large enough to cover the shame of killing innocent people for a purpose which is unattainable.
author: Howard Zinn

text: One certain effect of war is to diminish freedom of expression. Patriotism becomes the order of the day, and those who question the war are seen as traitors, to be silenced and imprisoned.
author: Howard Zinn

text: Voting is easy and marginally useful, but it is a poor substitute for democracy, which requires direct action by concerned citizens.
author: Howard Zinn

text: I am supposing, or perhaps only hoping, that our future may be found in the past's fugitive moments of compassion rather than in its solid centuries of warfare.
author: Howard Zinn
source: A People's History of the United States (1980)

text: Capitalism has always been a failure for the lower classes. It is now beginning to fail for the middle classes.
author: Howard Zinn
source: A People's History of the United States (1980; 2003)

text: Hence it is evident that the state is a creation of nature, and that man is by nature a political animal.
author: Aristotle
source: Politics, Book I (c. 350 BC), trans. Benjamin Jowett

text: For one swallow does not make a summer, nor does one day; and so too one day, or a short time, does not make a man blessed and happy.
author: Aristotle
source: Nicomachean Ethics, Book I (c. 350 BC), trans. W. D. Ross

text: And happiness is thought to depend on leisure; for we are busy that we may have leisure, and make war that we may live in peace.
author: Aristotle
source: Nicomachean Ethics, Book X (c. 350 BC), trans. W. D. Ross

text: Hence also it is no easy task to be good.
author: Aristotle
source: Nicomachean Ethics, Book II (c. 350 BC), trans. W. D. Ross

text: All men by nature desire to know.
author: Aristotle
source: Metaphysics, Book I (c. 350 BC), trans. W. D. Ross

text: A whole is that which has a beginning, a middle, and an end.
author: Aristotle
source: Poetics, part VII (c. 335 BC), trans. S. H. Butcher

text: Poetry, therefore, is a more philosophical and a higher thing than history: for poetry tends to express the universal, history the particular.
author: Aristotle
source: Poetics, part IX (c. 335 BC), trans. S. H. Butcher

text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 1, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 5, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 81, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 103, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord?
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 160, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 165, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: Health is the greatest of gifts, contentedness the best riches; trust is the best of relationships, Nirvana the highest happiness.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 204, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 223, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)

text: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers.
author: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha)
source: Dhammapada, verse 276, trans. F. Max Muller (1881)
